title: Destructuring & spread
description: Pull values out of arrays/objects in one line, and splat or collect with `...`.

notes: Spread is SHALLOW — nested objects/arrays still share references.
`...rest` must be the LAST element in destructuring or in a parameter list.
On object spread, later keys overwrite earlier ones.

questions.explain: The leading comma is a hole skipping index 0.

questions.q: After `const o = {...a, ...b}` with conflicting keys, which value wins?
options: Whichever value is non-undefined; both defined → TypeError on duplicate key
The one whose key was defined first across both objects' insertion order
Yes — spread recursively clones nested arrays and objects
Deep for arrays, shallow for objects inside
Deep only when the array has no cycles; throws on circular refs
Anywhere — `[...rest, last]` collects all but the last element
Anywhere, but holes (commas) before it are silently dropped
At the start or end, but never in the middle

L3.prompt: Write `sumAll(...args)` returning the sum of any number of arguments. Log `sumAll(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)`.
